newsitem.title: USA: Clinton untroubled by Democratic Party debts.
newsitem.headline: Clinton untroubled by Democratic Party debts.

text.p: President Clinton said Thursday he was not worried by the Democratic Party's deep debts from the 1996 campaign and would help it pay them off.
"I'm not particularly concerned about it. I think we will pay it back," Clinton told reporters at a White House event on health care.

Clinton said that the $14.4 million debt racked up by the Democratic National Committee, the party's main institution, had been expected and was needed to compete with a Republican party that historically far outraises the Democrats.
"Last year, when it became obvious that our congressional candidates were going to be outspent massively, we did everything we could to raise quite a good deal of money at the end," Clinton said.

"The committees and the Democratic committee went into debt with money that they could legally borrow in the hope of trying to be competitive, and they actually did a pretty good job. They were still outspent, I figure, in the last 10 days, two weeks, probably four or five to one," he added.
"But we knew that would happen and we knew it would take some time to pay it back," he said.
Clinton, who drummed up money for the party at scores of fund-raising events in last year's campaign, said he would do more on the party's behalf to help it retire the debt.
A Democratic official, confirming a New York Times report, said the party had $14.4 million in debt, faced projected legal bills of $4 million but had only $1.7 million on hand.

The official also said DNC did not have the resources to repay $1.5 million in unlawful or questionable contributions it has promised to return. Despite the controversy surrounding the party's fund-raising, Clinton has continued to raise money on its behalf this year, although his knee injury two weeks ago forced him to skip a California fund-raiser this week.
